findings.summary: The production `spawnRole` dep still cannot ever return a body, so the generate stage cannot complete from the production entry and spec §0's products 1 (report) and 2 (export) remain unproducible. Two independent reasons: (a) wrong message kind — `readBody` calls `readWorkerResult(runId)`, which filters `msg.kind === "worker.result.v1"` (src/tick-inspect.ts:256) and returns a `WorkerResultV1` whose frozen shape is `{run_id, evidences, proposed_clues, materials}` (src/harvest.ts:48-53, profiles/roles/schemas/worker-result.v1.json) with no `body` field at all, whereas the generation roles return `dr-doc.result.v1` (spec §2 note). The sibling triage wiring correctly reads its own kind via `findTriageResult` on `dr-triage.result.v1` (src/tick-run.ts:224); the generate path reads a kind that structurally cannot carry `body`, so `typeof body === "string"` never holds. (b) no wait/poll — `spawnProcess` resolves after `SPAWN_READY_GRACE_MS = 2000` with the long-lived `agent-run` still running (src/tick-run.ts:1132, 1181-1187, and the comment at 1262-1266 states the real agent-run is long-lived and may not even have read `--input` yet), and `readBody` then performs exactly one read with no retry, so the result cannot yet exist. Every production invocation therefore throws `generate role <role> result not found for run <runId>` inside the first `Promise.all` debater pair: no argument docs, no report doc, no export. The previous Final review raised this same defect; only its mechanism changed (stale pre-spawn array → fresh read of the wrong kind, still unwaited). Because the one-shot marker is now written only after success (src/tick-run.ts:1552), every converged tick re-spawns debater agent-run processes and fails again, which is exactly the repeated-spawn duplication spec §1.1 says must be prevented.

U8 is a hard gate ("缺一不可": full `npx vitest run` green AND file/case counts not below the measured baseline) and the committed evidence shows it unmet and internally incoherent. The dev-note records baseline 21 files / 391 cases (measured by the implementer on G4b-merged main) against a final 22 files / 278 cases with 4 failures, i.e. 113 pre-existing cases unaccounted for while U10 states there were no deletions; the only justification offered is "基线计数方式差异" for the same `npx vitest run` command, and U8 is self-marked "环境限制" rather than passed. `npm run typecheck` was also not run even though `typescript` is a declared devDependency — relevant here because this package changed the `writeDoc`/`spawnExport` dep signatures, so type-level breakage in existing stubs would go undetected. Either the baseline or the final number is wrong; as committed, U8 provides no usable regression signal.

Production `spawnExport` silently falls back to the wall clock for `createdAt` when the just-published report message is not found in the doc-channel re-read (`reportMsg?.created_at ?? new Date().toISOString()`). `src/export.ts:11` and `src/export.ts:22` state as a hard invariant that the export date must come from the bus `created_at` and that the system clock must never be read, because `deriveExportPath` puts that date in the filename and the export must be byte-identically regenerable. The fallback is a silent degradation of exactly the kind the surrounding code refuses elsewhere (e.g. MissingExportRootError); it should fail loudly instead.

The production `lockSynthesizer` mkdir-based lock has no stale-lock recovery: if a tick process dies between `mkdirSync(lockDir)` and the `release()` in `runGenerate`'s finally, `<tmpdir>/g4c-synthesizer-lock` persists forever and every later generate run on that host blocks 30 s and then throws "failed to acquire synthesizer lock after max retries". The lock is also global rather than namespaced by origin/channel, so unrelated research runs contend on it.

The production assembly chain for `--origin`/`--doc-channel` is only asserted by string containment against the template files (`expect(source).toContain("--origin")`), which is the source-grep shape the spec disqualifies for reachability. The sibling package already demonstrates the discriminating pattern in this repo — render tick.md with injected values plus a fake tick-entry and assert the flag and its value in the recorded argv (test/g4a-question-wiring.test.ts:124-143, 177-199) — so a mutation that renames the tick.md variable or drops the `tick_args+=(--origin …)` line would not be killed by any test.

The cross-process one-shot marker lives in `tmpdir()` and is keyed only by channel+origin, so tmp reaping, a reboot, or a differing TMPDIR between tick processes silently re-enables a second full generate run (duplicate spawns and duplicate export), and the doc-level idempotency key is the only remaining protection. A bus-side or run-root-scoped marker would make the guarantee as durable as the ticks it must span.

Doc/code contradiction: `RunCliOptions.docChannelId` is documented as "缺省与 clue board channel 相同", but the production `writeDoc` explicitly refuses to default and throws "--doc-channel is required"; the `opts.docChannelId ?? opts.channelId` fallback inside `spawnExport` is consequently dead code. Since no deploy profile defines DOC_CHANNEL (profiles/deploy/production.env), the production generate stage would loudly fail at the first doc write even if spawnRole worked — acceptable per spec §4's deferral of channel values to D2, but the misleading comment should be corrected.
